messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Things feel like they’re holding together, but just barely—like a stack of books someone’s leaning on, not a wall. The usual players are still in place, but even the most loyal ones seem to be watching their step a little more than usual. Let’s keep our ears open and our plans loose—this could tip either way if the wrong person stumbles."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels lighter than it has in months—checkpoints are quiet, the elites are betting on the long game, and even the schools are running like normal. But don’t be fooled: the doctors and teachers are whispering in corners, and the bureaucracy is grinding slower than ever. If the regime’s confidence is real, it’s still fragile—if it’s a show, it’s a good one. Stay sharp, but don’t panic. We’ll know soon enough which way the wind is blowing."*"
Sender 3: "*"Things feel like they’re shifting—less like the usual noise and more like something’s actually moving, but no one’s sure which way. The regime’s still in charge, but the cracks are showing in weird ways—some people are bracing, others are acting like nothing’s wrong, and the security forces? They’re following orders, but you can tell they’re watching the walls too."*"
Sender 4: "*"Things seem quieter than they have in a while—almost too quiet. The usual signs of trouble aren’t there, but the fact that they’re upgrading systems instead of just patching things up makes me wonder what they’re preparing for. Let’s keep our ears open, but no need to panic yet."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—even the landlord’s asking about exit plans now. The regime’s holding, but it’s holding *tighter*, not stronger. Let’s keep our eyes open, but our mouths shut—this isn’t the time to test the wind."*"
Sender 6: "*"The reshuffle reversal and the warehouse moves tell me they’re not panicking—they’re just tightening the screws. People are too busy making summer plans to think this is about to blow up, but if anyone’s waiting for a spark, they’re going to be disappointed. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are still standing, but the foundation’s shifting—even the ones who usually know everything are admitting they can’t see the full picture. The regime’s script is tighter than ever, but the cracks are in the things they can’t control: the quiet stalls, the oversubscribed bonds, the shopkeeper who finally said what we’ve all been thinking. For now, the game stays the same—but the players are starting to glance at the exits."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just more paint. The kids are singing the same songs we used to whisper, and even the neighbor’s new roof says they’re not packing. But the air feels like the calm before the storm, not the quiet after. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers of panic, just the same old machine humming along. Even the usual cracks in the system (you know the ones) are just... paperwork. No one’s holding their breath for a miracle, and honestly? Neither should we."*"
Sender 10: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but it’s the quiet before something—not sure what yet. The usual backroom deals are missing, the security guys are saving their energy, and even the markets seem to know not to get too excited. Stay sharp, but don’t do anything stupid—this isn’t the time to test the waters."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are being papered over—not patched. The old guard’s gone quiet, the soldiers are chatting with neighbors instead of barking orders, and the money’s flowing into new projects like nothing’s wrong. Football matches are packed, the pension checks cleared on time, and the diplomats are suddenly *very* curious about ‘what-ifs.’ No one’s moving yet, but the regime’s betting we won’t either. For now, they’re right."*"
Sender 12: "*"Looks like the walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers slipping through. Even the air feels heavier, like they’ve tightened the screws just enough that no one dares breathe too loud. Stay sharp, but keep your heads down—this isn’t the time for reckless moves."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are solid, the guards are relaxed, and the kids are singing the same songs as the adults—no cracks, just echoes. We’re not invisible, but for now, the system’s too busy watching itself to notice us."*"
Sender 14: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath but pretending it’s just a quiet day. The usual channels are still moving, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Let’s keep our ears open and our steps light."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels different—like something’s holding its breath. The usual signs are there, but quieter, like the regime is trying to keep the lights on while the walls shake. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this could go either way, and we don’t want to be the ones who misread the moment."*"
Sender 16: "*"Just saw the latest from the clinic—nothing unusual, just the usual flu season. And that logistics firm? They’re locking in long-term deals like nothing’s changing. Seems like the usual noise is just that—noise. But let’s keep our ears open, just in case."*"
Sender 17: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—stronger than ever, actually. The cracks we’ve been watching? Mostly just echoes now. People are settling in, and the regime’s not even sweating it. Still, keep your eyes open—just in case the quiet’s hiding something we haven’t seen yet."*"
Sender 18: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. Everyone’s keeping their heads down, the markets are quiet, and even the usual cracks in the script have been patched up. No one’s saying it out loud, but the message is clear: no one’s moving, no one’s testing. Still, we all know what happens when the wind changes—let’s stay sharp, but not so sharp it draws eyes."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are holding, but the cracks are getting harder to hide—just not where you’d expect. The usual suspects are still in their seats, but the air in the room feels thinner, like everyone’s holding their breath a little longer. Keep your circles tight, your ears open, and your hands steady—this isn’t the time to bet on weakness, but it’s also not the time to assume it’s unshakable."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the way they’re stocking the warehouses and the way the soldiers are smiling at us instead of glaring? That’s not kindness. It’s a sign they’re ready to move fast if they have to. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 21: "*"The air feels heavy but still—like the calm before nothing. The usual whispers have gone quiet, even the ones we thought we could trust, and the only thing moving is the clock. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open, but don’t mistake the silence for safety."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers of weakness. Even the usual grumblers are quiet, but not out of fear, it seems. The regime’s got its house in order, and for now, the game is theirs to play. Keep your heads down, but stay sharp—this calm might just be the eye of the storm."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels heavy, like everyone’s holding their breath—no one’s celebrating, but no one’s running for the exits yet. The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching a building with cracks in the foundation: no one’s sure when—or if—it’ll come down, but the smart ones are quietly checking their escape routes."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels different—less like the usual script, more like a game where no one’s sure who’s holding the cards. The jokes are sharper, the mistakes are piling up, and even the traders are acting like they’re waiting for the other shoe to drop. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could tip either way, and we don’t want to be the ones who misread the moment."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The usual channels are quiet, but the cracks are in the mortar, not the stone. Keep your heads down, but don’t let the market fool you—plenty of people are betting on the roof not caving in, but the foundation’s shifting under the floorboards."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
